requirements.title: Machine-checked catalog↔corpus fidelity — the diagram catalog can never over-claim
requirements.notes: Catalog audit dimension #4 (auditability) graded C: the Build plan promised '≈34 example models now' but only 27 non-showcase examples shipped, ~14 named ✅/◐ rows were ABSENT, and NOTHING machine-checked the catalog vs the corpus. IMPLEMENTED by ADR-0027: a structured manifest `examples/catalog.json` (each shipped diagram = a row {file,type,family,name,catalogId?}; the ◇ new-types listed separately as newTypes with no example) + `conformance/catalog.test.ts` asserting (i) every diagrams[].file exists, parses, and model.diagram===type (a real renderer type); (ii) every non-showcase examples/*.psyuml is listed EXACTLY ONCE (no orphan/dup); (iii) each showcase-<type>.psyuml is a real type matching its model; (iv) manifest count===shipped count; (v) newTypes documented + never shipped. So a 'ships now' claim can never again be untrue of the corpus — the catalog joins the goldens/invariants as CHECKED. Green over the now-37 non-showcase + 12 showcase corpus. The prose diagram-catalog.md build-count is corrected to point at the manifest; full prose↔manifest unification is REQ-CATALOG-METADATA.

requirements.title: Close the catalog drift + the canonical coverage gaps
requirements.notes: Catalog audit dimensions #2 (coverage) + #4 (drift). DONE (ADR-0027): 18 new examples shipped across two batches, each authored to pass EVERY existing invariant (validate both layers, overlap ADR-0012, legibility, layout-quality ADR-0021, edge↔edge ADR-0025) and registered in examples/catalog.json — 45 non-showcase examples now. Batch 1 (10): safety-behaviour (#5), reciprocal-roles (#13), dilemma (#11), snag (#12); health-anxiety, ptsd-cycle/Ehlers–Clark, metacognitive-cas/Wells; sorc (#43), abc (#44); trauma-timeline (#34). Batch 2 (8): eating-disorder/Fairburn, psychosis-cycle/Morrison [the remaining disorder-specific maintenance models]; empowerment-triangle (#19), structural-dissociation (#17 ANP/EP); ecomap (#22), social-atom (#23), cultural-genogram (#24) [relational-field, hand-laid-out planar star/family layouts]; narrative-externalising/White. Authoring rules learned + recorded in ADR-0027: a loop's EXIT must leave the same node the loop-closing edge does (else the exit chord crosses); relational-field star layouts (person + radial systems/others) are naturally planar. Confirmed ritual.psyuml IS the grief ritual (#48+#49 — not drift). OUT OF SCOPE as a single file: a standalone COMPOSITE example — renderComposite takes an ARRAY of models, not a single .psyuml of type 'composite' (no such renderer type); it is demoed live in the editor's Composite board, and a persisted multi-document case file is REQ-CASE-FILE (M21). GALLERY WIRED: all 18 new examples are now browsable in the editor's family-grouped picker (apps/web), each with its honest one-line note; the gallery's example sources moved to a Vite glob (`import.meta.glob` over examples/*.psyuml) so the picker auto-includes any shipped example (57 items now) — adding an example no longer needs an App.tsx import. Nothing left outstanding for COVERAGE.

requirements.title: Consistent per-item catalog schema + navigation (safety/cultural caveat, citations, picture audience, cross-refs)
requirements.notes: Catalog audit dimensions #3 (metadata consistency) + #5 (structure). PASS 1 (prose): the audience KEY now defines the product's THREE profiles (clinician/client/PICTURE, ADR-0016) + a picture-suitability rule; a consolidated SAFETY & CULTURAL CAVEATS section (suicide/crisis, trauma/dissociation, psychosis, sharing-harm, cultural, contested-theory); a REFERENCES section; a Contents overview + 'see also' cross-refs (41↔53, 18↔19, 43↔44↔55, 9/13↔58) + items 52–59 folded into families. PASS 2 (SINGLE SOURCE, ADR-0028): examples/catalog.json is now the single source for the shipped library — each `diagrams` row carries the full schema {file,type,family,name,school,note,audience∈C|L|B}; `scripts/build-catalog.mjs` GENERATES the catalog's per-family 'Shipped example library' table from it (drift-checked by conformance/catalog.test.ts — the committed table is parsed back and asserted equal to the manifest, content-compared so Prettier alignment is irrelevant); the editor gallery (App.tsx) DERIVES its non-showcase items from the same manifest (removed ~250 hand-written entries; ★ showcase stays a small list); conformance enforces the schema (school/note non-empty, audience valid). So the prose table, the gallery, and the corpus cannot drift — all flow from one checked manifest. REMAINING (deferred, not blocking): generating the rich 59-row FAMILY tables too (they include non-shipped ◇ rows + survey prose — a larger model change) and cross-linking each notation glyph to the M14 set.

requirements.title: Persisted multi-document composite 'case file' + editor composite authoring
requirements.notes: Implemented additively (ADR-0039). A `CaseFile` schema in `@psyuml/model` — `{ version, kind: 'case-file', meta: { title?, note? }, documents: PsyumlModel[] }` — is a PURE container (each document is a fully-validated `PsyumlModel`, so NEVER a model-schema change); the `kind: 'case-file'` literal discriminates a case file from a single model so `parseCaseFile` rejects the latter. `parseCaseFile`/`serializeCaseFile` round-trip losslessly; `caseFileFrom(documents, meta)` builds one. The editor's Composite board IS the documents: the panel gains a case-title field, Save case file (`<slug>.psyuml-case`), Open case file (repopulates board + title, shows the composite), and a per-view list with Remove — real authoring, not just append/clear; `renderComposite(board)` unchanged (the board was always `PsyumlModel[]`). HONEST SCOPE: a case file aggregates several views of one person → MORE IDENTIFYING; §L.2 disclaimer + de-identification (REQ-PRIVACY/`toFhir`) unchanged + applied per document (no new PII handling). Authoring is snapshot-based (a board view is a copy); in-place view editing + reorder-by-drag are future polish; no CLI surface yet. Verified by a model round-trip/discrimination unit test + a Playwright e2e (author 2 views → save → clear → reopen → board repopulates).

requirements.title: Live §K profile + cultural-pack loading/applying in the editor
requirements.notes: Implemented in the editor (ADR-0040), reusing the existing §K machinery with NO new validation. A Profile (§K) file input + two Try quick-loads (`CFT_PROFILE`/`CULTURAL_PACK_EXAMPLE`); `applyProfile` runs `validateProfile` (the four §K rules + Tier-1 freeze + glyph-collision + the §6 `profile.cultural-permission` rule) and applies the profile's `roleLabelsFromProfile` vocabulary to `render` ONLY IF `ok` — an invalid / un-permitted profile (a `restricted` symbol with no `permission`) is shown with its errors and NEVER applied (the §6 gate enforced in the UI). The applied vocabulary uses the SAME `roleLabels` surface as the built-in `school` selector (disabled while a profile is active). A profile panel surfaces the applied profile + every validation issue + (leading) each cultural stereotype's tradition/RESTRICTED/permission/attribution. HONEST SCOPE: 'apply' = the cross-school VOCABULARY (labels), not per-stereotype custom glyphs (the renderer is glyph-by-type — future); profiles are session-only (not persisted into the model/case file, keeping the permission boundary clean). `validateProfile` itself is already unit-tested in the profiles suite; a Playwright e2e applies the cultural pack + asserts the §6 RESTRICTED permission shows + that reverting restores the built-in path.

requirements.title: Real multi-language label packs + RTL + editor locale switch (the architecture exists; the content does not)
requirements.notes: Implemented as the MECHANISM + one illustrative demo pack (ADR-0042); the REQ-I18N architecture (concept ids vs localized labels) is now USABLE. `@psyuml/model`: `isRtl(lang)` (RTL base subtags ar/he/fa/ur/yi/ps/sd) + `availableLanguages(model)` (the langs a model's labels actually carry, `model.language` first, de-duped). Editor: a Language selector listing those langs (disabled when monolingual); `activeLang` flows to `render`/`renderComposite` + `getText` localizes; clamped to a language the model has; an RTL locale sets `dir="rtl"` on the diagram container (browser bidi shaping). One demo pack `examples/i18n-demo.psyuml` (a generic process-loop in en · es · ar) exercises it; its disclaimer states the translations are basic + NOT professionally validated. HONEST SCOPE (recorded): clinical content is NEVER machine/AI-translated and shipped as usable — hence one marked-illustrative pack, not 73 fabricated translations; renderer CHROME stays English (safety 'EXIT', ladder 'harder/easier', banners, legends — only model content localizes); RTL is text-direction, not geometry mirroring; `meta.title`/`disclaimer` are monolingual strings. Model unit tests (`isRtl`, `availableLanguages`) + a Playwright e2e (en→es labels change; en→ar labels change AND `dir` flips to rtl; back to en → ltr). Localizing renderer chrome (a string table across 20 renderers) is the honest remaining gap.

requirements.title: Represent HOW contested schools disagree, not only which (the ⚖ narrative)
requirements.notes: Implemented (ADR-0041), the 'how' behind ADR-0007's ⚖ 'which'. A new optional `Properties.provenanceNote` (ADDITIVE) captures HOW the schools in `provenance` differ on an element. `renderPartsMap` draws it as a footnote above the legend (`⚖ <name>: <note>`, plain text — not `data-el`, so overlap is untouched; the parts-map height content-fits) AND appends it to alt-text (`How they differ — …`), both gated to the clinician/interpretive surface (client/picture hide it); the ⚖ marker (which) is unchanged and nothing is merged (§G.2 upheld). `validate` adds an `info` nudge `provenance.narrative-missing` when a contested node lacks a note (never blocks, mirrors `provenance.node-mixed-school`). Free text (one short narrative), not a structured per-school table — disagreements aren't always a clean A-says-X/B-says-Y split. The showcase parts-map's contested 'inner critic' carries a real note (+golden); covered by a render test (visible footnote + alt-text, gated), a validate test (the nudge, satisfied by a note), + model parse. HONEST SCOPE: the visible footnote is parts-map only (the canonical contested renderer, ADR-0007); the loop-map gets the field + alt-text path, its footnote a follow-up.

requirements.title: Raster / print export (PNG, PDF, print stylesheet)
requirements.notes: Implemented dependency-free (ADR-0038). `downloadPng` rasterizes the deterministic SVG IN THE BROWSER — read the viewBox, draw into an <Image>, paint onto a <canvas> at 2× over an opaque white ground, `canvas.toBlob('image/png')` → download (the SVG has no external refs → untainted canvas); an Export PNG button beside Export SVG, behind the same `exportBlocked` health gate, filename from the title slug. A Print button + an `@media print` block (styles.css) hide the editor chrome and print the diagram + its honest 'about' caption — the diagram SVG already draws the disclaimer, so the standing disclaimer/crisis copy travels onto the page (§L.2 gating unchanged); browser Save-as-PDF is the PDF path (NO rasterizer/PDF library bundled — ADR-0013 no-new-dep). The active audience profile is preserved (export uses the on-screen `svg`). HONEST SCOPE: PNG is browser-only (canvas) — the CLI still emits SVG only; 'PDF' is print-to-PDF, not a generated file. A Playwright e2e captures the download + asserts a real PNG (8-byte signature + non-trivial size).

requirements.title: Documentation factual claims stay consistent with the system + with itself (un-driftable)
requirements.notes: Implemented (ADR-0043) as a machine-checked drift guard, mirroring the catalog↔corpus pattern (ADR-0027/0028) but for the PROSE docs. `conformance/docs-conformance.test.ts` derives the load-bearing facts from the SYSTEM — `DiagramType.options` (the renderer count + the exact type list), `FAMILIES.length` (the family count), and the `examples/` corpus (one `showcase-<type>.psyuml` per type) — and asserts the docs match: (1) the format-reference 'Diagram types — authoring quick-guide' table lists EXACTLY `DiagramType.options` (a missing/extra renderer row fails CI); (2) every digit-form 'N diagram types/renderers' claim across the live docs + package IMPACTs equals the renderer count; (3) every digit-form 'N families' claim equals `FAMILIES.length`; (4) there is exactly one `showcase-<type>` per type. So the drift a human had to reconcile by hand (a doc saying '12 diagram types', a quick-guide missing the 8 new ◇ renderers) can never silently return. Also reconciled the pre-existing drift the audit found (format-reference quick-guide completed to 20 rows; the v0.2 spec, roadmap-to-v1, ROADMAP, ARCHITECTURE, render/profiles IMPACTs counts + statuses brought current). HONEST SCOPE: the guard checks DIGIT-form counts (`12`, `20`), not spelled-out words ('eight families' is prose, unchecked — catching it risks false positives like 'one of the families'); a `(?<![.\w])` lookbehind excludes version/identifier digits ('v0.1 diagram types', 'v0.2 families', 'M15') which are not counts; the dated cited-research archive (`docs/research/**`, its own drift check) and append-only ADR history (`sdd/adr/**`) are out of scope by design.

requirements.title: A polished, drift-proof printable HTML showcase: worked diagrams + explanations + an on-paper usage guide
requirements.notes: Implemented (ADR-0044) as a single-source, drift-locked, self-contained page. `examples/showcase.json` is the single source — per diagram type, editorial prose only (`oneLiner`/`whatItShows`/`whenToUse`/`onPaper`/`evidenceNote`/`school`/`audience`/`family`) + page-level content (the four JTBD jobs, a reading guide, an ON-PAPER drawing guide, the honesty notes, and a family chooser). It does NOT duplicate system facts: each diagram's TITLE is pulled from its model, the RENDER from the committed golden `examples/showcase-<type>.svg`, and `family`/the chooser are checked against `FAMILY_OF`/`FAMILIES`. `scripts/build-showcase.mjs` (pure `renderShowcase` + `esc` exported for the test; `main()` does the IO) emits `apps/web/public/showcase.html` — inline CSS + inline SVG, NO external assets — framed as four jobs-to-be-done (read it / draw it on paper / choose the right one / use it honestly), grouped by family, with a sticky family nav, per-diagram cards (the render is the hero; explanation, when-to-use, on-paper steps + a green honest note below), light/dark theming, and a PRINT stylesheet so the page itself prints onto paper. Runs in `dev`/`build` after build-docs.mjs; output gitignored like handbook.html/diagram-catalog.html. Linked from the editor's intro note (base-aware). TDD: `conformance/showcase.test.ts` (written first, red before the generator) checks the manifest vs the system (`diagrams` == `DiagramType.options` one-per-type; `family` == `FAMILY_OF`; chooser == `FAMILIES`; substantive prose + committed golden/model per entry) AND the generated page vs the manifest (self-contained; inlines every render + each REAL model title; carries every explanation/on-paper guide/JTBD job/chooser question/honesty note); `apps/web/links.test.ts` generates + link-checks it. HONEST SCOPE: one example per type (the feature-dense `showcase-<type>` models), not the 40+ catalogue; the drift guard locks structure + coverage, not the hand-authored wording (evidence notes deliberately separate well-evidenced therapies from useful-but-unproven diagrams); `pattern`/`composite` have no renderer yet and are shown honestly in the chooser; no new runtime dependency.

requirements.title: No two rendered words collide — the chrome/caption text overlap gap is machine-checked
requirements.notes: Implemented (ADR-0045). The overlap invariant (ADR-0012) only guards the `data-el` NODE/LABEL boxes, so UNTAGGED chrome text — the diagram title, band/lane headers, per-region contents, captions, provenance footnotes, legends — could collide unseen (a visual audit of the showcase found 14 such pairs across 12 corpus files, in 5 classes). `introspect.textBoxesFromSvg` now reconstructs the AABB of EVERY `<text>` element (halos are a white stroke on the same element, so each word is counted once), and `packages/render/text-overlap.test.ts` asserts no two text boxes overlap for every `examples/*.psyuml` in BOTH audience layers. Five renderer fixes made the corpus clean: (1) `renderInterventionSeq` reserves a title band so the title can't overlap the lane headers (6 files); (2) `renderLoopMap` reserves the centre R/B + loop-topology badge as a `deCollide` obstacle so chord-midpoint edge labels avoid it (3 files); (3) `renderVenn` caps each region's contents descriptor to its zone's share of the centre-spacing (textLength); (4) `renderPartsMap` widens the gap between the provenance footnote and the legend; (5) `renderResourceMap` caps each column header to its column. 11 goldens regenerated; the full render+conformance suite stays green. HONEST SCOPE: text↔text only — text drawn OVER decoration (a region banner on a circle, a sensation label on a body outline, an edge label on its own connector) is intentional labelling and is NOT a collision (decoration is not a `<text>`); text staying inside its own container shape is the separate containment guarantee (REQ-TEXT-CONTAINMENT, ADR-0046).

requirements.title: Rendered text stays inside its own container shape — no caption/label clipped by its box/circle/oval
requirements.notes:
Made UNIVERSAL (ADR-0051): the last caption-bisection exception (CAPTION_BISECT_KNOWN_GAP = {decision-nav}, the deferred ADR-0046 graze) is closed on the SAFETY-CRITICAL crisis node. The '! Call a crisis line now' box's crisis-resources caption had its TOP line riding up under the thick bottom border — root cause a CENTRING bug, not lack of room: `wrapLabel` centres its block, so the fixed `+13` offset placed the 3-line block's top line ~1px below the box bottom (ascenders inside the border); and under the ADR-0049 layered layout the depth-2 boxes sit in the centre/right lanes (not below the left crisis node), leaving ~20px unused. Fix: shift the caption block DOWN by half its height (cy = boxBottom + 13 + (lines-1)*lh/2) so the first line always clears the border whatever the line count (measured box bottom y=185 -> caption top y~191). `decision-nav` removed from the known-gap, so layout-quality invariant C now enforces 'every node caption is clear of its node border' for EVERY renderer x both layers (the sibling-collision ADR-0046 worried about is now actively machine-checked by overlap + text-overlap + C, not asserted away); 2 goldens regenerated (decision-nav, showcase-decision-nav).

Extended (ADR-0050) to the non-rectangular DIAMOND shape: a dense-diagram audit (ADR-0049 follow-up) found the process-loop RESOURCE node — a flat 140x44 rhombus (the 'way out' / exit target) — drew its label INSIDE at the rect width, so any label needing more than one line (or a single line wider than the narrow inscribed band) poked through the slanted edges (a rhombus has its full width only on its centre line; the panic-cycle clinician exit label was cut by the lower edges). The diamond CAN'T grow (the ring layout assumes the shared LNODE 140x44 footprint — growing it produced 19 overlap.test failures), and two lines can't be inscribed in a 44px-tall rhombus. Fix: place the label by LENGTH — a SHORT label (textWidth <= 100px, one line) stays INSIDE the widest band (the diamond reads as a normal filled node, e.g. client 'Ride it out'); a LONG label is lifted OUTSIDE on the OUTWARD vertical side (above the diamond when it sits in the ring's upper half, below otherwise, from the ring centroid), wrapped to <=3 lines at full node width, white-haloed (ADR-0047) so it stays legible over any chord, with the content-fit frame grown past it. The outward side is open exterior AND the side away from the incoming exit chord (whose own midpoint label is on the inward side), so the node label never collides with the edge label. GUARD: `legibility.test.ts` asserts that for every loop-map resource node, both layers, every label line is either WHOLLY inside the rhombus (all 4 corners satisfy |x-cx|/HW + |y-cy|/HH <= 1) or WHOLLY clear of the diamond box — never half-in cutting an edge; TDD, proven red on 18 layer-cases when forced inside, green as shipped. 8 process-loop goldens regenerated. HONEST SCOPE: a future ring hemmed on a diamond's outward side is caught by the overlap/text-overlap invariants, not silently shipped.

Implemented (ADR-0046), the companion to REQ-TEXT-LEGIBILITY for the OTHER showcase-audit class: text clipped by its OWN container shape. The clear defect — `renderModeMap` mode names overflowing their dominance-sized circles — is fixed by moving the name + `dom` numeral to a caption BELOW the circle, so the circle is a PURE dominance glyph (nothing to clip; better notation — 0.85 biggest → 0.30 smallest reads cleanly) and the name (now an outside caption) is covered by the ADR-0045 text↔text invariant against its neighbours. The guard: `layout-quality.test.ts` invariant C asserts every node label whose CENTRE is outside its node is DISJOINT from it (never straddling the border), every example × both layers — so combined with invariant A (centre-inside ⇒ contained, ADR-0021) every owner label is cleanly IN or OUT, never bisected; the mode-map fix is now machine-guarded. HONEST SCOPE: interior glyph-label tightness (parts-map / relational-field labels filling their symbol nodes) is the INTENDED notation and stays within invariant A's 3px slop — not a defect, not in scope (forcing strict margins would flag the intended design + risk node-overlap from growing every glyph). `CAPTION_BISECT_KNOWN_GAP = {decision-nav}` is the one documented exception (its crisis-resources caption grazes its thick-bordered node by ~6px in the deliberately compact crisis chart, where pushing it fully clear collides with a sibling branch label — a worse defect; it is the node's OWN caption and stays legible). Text-over-DECORATION (secure-base banner on the circle, body-map labels on the body outline) stays intentional + out of scope (ADR-0045). 2 mode-map goldens regenerated; full render+conformance suite green.

requirements.title: Every label over a line or decoration is haloed so the line never strikes through the text
requirements.notes: Implemented (ADR-0047). A pervasive low-grade legibility problem — a word drawn ON or beside a line read with the line striking through it (process-loop 'trigger', mode-map 'attacks'/'yields'/the dom numeral, two-triangles 'hides'/'stirs', intervention-sequence guards, relational-field ties, secure-base banners crossing the circle, body-map sensations crossing the outline) — fixed with the established white under-glyph halo (`paint-order="stroke"`), previously applied only ad hoc (4 of 8 raw edge labels; `fitText`/`wrapLabel` had no halo at all). Made the halo a first-class `TextOpts.halo` option of the shared `fitText`/`wrapLabel` helpers (+ `haloAttr`) and applied it to every edge label + every over-decoration node label (secure-base banners, body-map sensations, mode-map name/dom/'↑ grow', relational-field genogram person labels whose tie-lines pass through them). GUARD: `legibility.test.ts` asserts every `data-el="edgelabel:"` carries `paint-order="stroke"` for every example × both layers (edge labels are the universal connector-borne case), so a future bare edge label fails CI. Purely additive (white stroke under existing glyphs) — geometry unchanged, so overlap/containment/crossing invariants untouched and `legibility.test.ts`'s microtext floor still holds; 25 goldens regenerated. HONEST SCOPE: the guard asserts edge labels specifically; over-decoration node-label halos are applied but not separately asserted (they aren't a uniform enumerable class like `edgelabel:`).

requirements.title: Open a specific diagram from a URL — the showcase's browse → edit flow
requirements.notes: Implemented (ADR-0048). The showcase let a newcomer browse a worked example of every type, but its only path into the editor landed on the default `state-map`, not the diagram being read — browse → edit was broken, and the editor had no URL handling. A pure, node-tested helper `exampleKeyFromQuery(search, available, fallback)` (apps/web/editor.ts) returns the `?example=<key>` value IF it names a shipped example, else the fallback (unknown/garbage/path-injection-looking keys fall back safely — only exact known keys load); App.tsx resolves it once at mount from `window.location.search` for the initial model, and `loadModel` mirrors the current example into the URL via `history.replaceState` (a New/Open-file load clears the param) so the open diagram is shareable / bookmarkable / refresh-stable. Each showcase card gains an 'Open this diagram in the editor →' link to `./?example=showcase-<type>` (base-aware: from /psyuml/showcase.html → /psyuml/?example=…, the editor); `conformance/showcase.test.ts` asserts the link per diagram. Verified end-to-end (Playwright: loading ?example=showcase-parts-map opens the parts-map showcase). HONEST SCOPE: deep-links target the shipped EXAMPLE corpus only (no remote/file fetch, no off-corpus load); `replaceState` not `pushState` (no history stack); a single query param, not a full router or model-in-URL (privacy).

requirements.title: Proper layered (Sugiyama) layout — crossing minimisation + aligned coordinates — for the flow diagram
requirements.notes: Implemented (ADR-0049). The decision-nav crisis chart did only Sugiyama steps 1-2 inline (cycle-break + longest-path), then ordered within-layer by MODEL order and centred each layer independently — skipping the two SOTA quality steps. New deterministic `packages/render/layered.ts` (`layeredLayout`) implements the full pipeline: cycle removal + longest-path rank, **crossing minimisation** (median heuristic over down/up sweeps, keep-best, + adjacent-transpose), and **coordinate assignment** (median alignment pulling each node toward its neighbours' median x with the VPSC `separate1D` enforcing order+gap — straightens parent→child edges; a convergence node now centres under its parents). Deterministic (original-index tie-breaks, stable sorts, fixed sweeps) so goldens stay stable. `renderDecisionChart` uses it; the old `layerWithCycleBreak` was deleted. Unit-tested (`layered.test.ts`: layering, cycle handling, crossing reduction proof, edge alignment, separation, determinism); the corpus geometry invariants (overlap, layout-quality A+B+C, crossing ≤ baseline) all hold — decision-nav stays crossing-free; 3 decision-nav-type goldens regenerated (decision-nav, showcase-decision-nav, act-choice-point). HONEST SCOPE: the coordinate step is a median/priority method, not full Brandes-Köpf (the gold-standard, noted as the future upgrade, mirroring `separate1D` = '1-D core' / full VPSC); long edges connect endpoint-to-endpoint (no dummy-node chains, so multi-layer crossing counts are approximate — fine at corpus scale); applies to the FREE-ordering layered diagram (decision-nav) — `intervention-sequence` is swimlane-constrained (x fixed by lane) and keeps its lane layout; force/stochastic layout is rejected (research Angle 4) as unfit for golden tests.

requirements.title: No rendered text spills past the viewBox — chrome text (title/caption/disclaimer/legend) stays in frame
requirements.notes:
Implemented (ADR-0052), the in-frame analogue of REQ-TEXT-LEGIBILITY (text<->text) and ADR-0012's box in-frame check. `overlap.test.ts` asserts every `data-el` box is inside the viewBox but is blind to UNTAGGED chrome text — the title, a guidance caption, the disclaimer, the genogram legend — so a line wider than the frame spilled past the viewBox and CLIPPED on export / in an embed with nothing to catch it. Found first on the body-map (its fixed 460px frame clipped the title AND both bottom chrome lines, the caption by ~220px), then a corpus sweep showed it was PERVASIVE: 38 layer-cases across ~10 renderers (every process-loop title — the ring content-fit ignores the title row; the genogram legend — a fixed reference strip wider than the node spread; many captions/disclaimers emitted as raw full-width <text>). FIX: a new invariant in `text-overlap.test.ts` reconstructs the AABB of EVERY <text> (`introspect.textBoxesFromSvg`, honouring textLength) and asserts it sits inside the SVG's own viewBox (every example x both layers, ~4px metric tolerance); plus a shared `chromeLine(s,x,y,frameW,opts)` helper that compresses a bottom chrome line to the frame width via fitText (byte-identical for non-overflowing lines, so they don't churn) — applied to the overflowing captions/disclaimers (mode-map, ladder, three-circles, venn, resource-anchor, schema-grid, decisional-balance, secure-base). Two cases get ROOM not compression: process-loop titles (the ring frame grows its width to fit the title) and the genogram legend+title (the frame grows to fit the glyph legend at full size); the body-map's long caption+disclaimer WRAP and its frame height grows (the ADR-0050 outside-the-glyph pattern applied to chrome). 16 goldens regenerated; all geometry invariants hold. HONEST SCOPE: the helper is applied where overflow exists today; other renderers' chrome is guarded by the invariant and converted lazily if it ever overflows (an accepted, invariant-backed raw/chromeLine inconsistency).

TITLE ROBUSTNESS (ADR-0052 follow-up): the corpus titles are short, so the in-frame invariant only proves THOSE fit — but a long user title clips in the LIVE EDITOR, where no in-frame test runs. The CONTENT-FIT renderers (whose frame is sized to nodes and ignores the title row) now grow their frame width to contain the title: process-loop + relational-field (the original ADR-0052 fixes) plus state-map, mode-map, two-triangles, parts-map and decision-nav — each a one-line `Math.max(existing..., titleW + pad)`, ZERO golden churn (current titles fit, so max picks the node width). GUARD: a `text-overlap.test.ts` case plants a 94-char title on each content-fit renderer and asserts it stays in frame (TDD, proven red when a growth term is dropped). The fixed-width renderers keep their wide frames (a title rarely exceeds them) and stay invariant-guarded.
